# Outlier

> Mac-native local AI runtime with a custom paged Mixture-of-
> Experts inference engine. Runs models up to
> Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on 64GB Apple Silicon Macs by streaming
> expert weights off SSD (about 2 tokens a second). Offline, no API tokens, no usage caps.
> Includes an agent loop (plan / act / verify /
> recover), MCP connectors, Projects, coding as a mode of the
> Core tier, and six model tiers from 4B to 397B.

Checked 2026-11-23 against the live site. Re-read and re-dated every 14 days.

## Is Outlier free?
Nano and Lite are free. No account.
Pro adds every model for $39 once. Black Friday sale: $16.99 once through December 2. Then $39. (The sale ends 2026-12-03 at 07:59 UTC.)
macOS 15+, Apple silicon. Runs on the Mac, works offline.
Refund window: 30 days, no questions asked. One payment, no subscription.

## Pricing
- Requirements: M1 or newer · macOS 15+ (free update)
- Free: Nano 4B + Lite 9B, no account, no token bill
- Pro: a one-time purchase, not a subscription - all six tiers including Plus 397B, Marathon mode, Computer use, Deep Research, context up to 128K tokens (Free: 8K). $39 once, activates on up to 3 Macs, 30-day money-back guarantee.
- Outlier Lifetime Licence. Black Friday sale: $16.99 once through December 2. Then $39. The sale lasts until 2026-12-03 07:59 UTC, the end of 2 December US Pacific; from 3 December $39. Checkout charges the sale price. Everything Pro includes for the lifetime of the Outlier product, including future model releases. If Outlier is ever sunset, licence holders get 90 days' notice and a final release.

## Who makes Outlier
Outlier is made by Kerr & Company (https://kerrandcompanyholdings.com/), Matthew Kerr, one person in Grand Rapids, Michigan (https://outlier.host/about/), who also makes Crisp Video (offline video restore for Mac) and Check Engine SEO (website audits).

## Models and the memory each needs
Six tiers. Free: Nano and Lite. Pro: the other four. A 16 GB MacBook Air runs both free models.
- Nano (Qwen3.5-4B, MLX 4-bit): free. 2.37 GB download, 6 GB minimum memory.
- Lite (Qwen3.5-9B, MLX 4-bit): free. 5.04 GB download, 12 GB minimum memory.
- Quick (Gemma 4 26B mixture of experts): Pro. 15.61 GB download, 16 GB minimum, 24 GB recommended. For reasoning, not positioned as a coding tier.
- Core (Qwen3.6-27B, text): Pro. 15.13 GB download, 24 GB minimum. Coding is a mode of Core.
- Vision 3.8 (Qwen3.8-27B, images and text): Pro. 15.5 GB download, 24 GB minimum.
- Plus (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, paged from the SSD): Pro. 209 GB of disk, 64 GB minimum, 128 GB recommended. About 2 tokens a second: for depth, not speed.
Check a specific Mac and model: https://outlier.host/will-it-run/ and https://outlier.host/data/mac-ram-to-model-size/

## Requirements
- A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) on macOS 15 or later (a free update). Intel Macs are not supported.
- No account. The free tiers need no payment and no sign-in.
- Windows: in testing, no date promised.

## What can leave your Mac (summary of https://outlier.host/privacy.html)
The model runs on the Mac and answers with the network off. Chats, memory and files stay on the Mac's disk.
- Three checks run on their own: the app update check (a GET to a public GitHub URL; updates are signed with minisign and verified before install), the licence re-check (at startup and once a day; if it can't reach the server, Pro keeps working), and the price check when you open an upgrade window (it names the site and nothing else).
- Only when you use the feature: model downloads from Hugging Face (the first time you use each tier), web search (your search query goes to DuckDuckGo, Mojeek and Wikipedia), Research (it needs web search on), a cloud model with your own API key, an MCP server or anything else you connect yourself, and licence activation (the key goes to the vendor that issued it).
- With web off, the agent has no web search, web pages or web-connected tools, and a command that downloads or installs from the internet asks you first, every time.

## Measured benchmarks (our runs on a 64 GB Mac Studio M1 Ultra, with dates)
- Nano decode: 92.6 tokens a second on Outlier 1.11.1020, three timed runs on 22 November 2026, with a peak of 5.5 to 5.8 GB of memory (https://outlier.host/data/local-ai-benchmarks-mac-2026/). The earlier round measured 71.7 (2026-04-29).
- Decode, earlier rounds: Lite 53.4 and Core 20.7 tokens a second (2026-04-29); Quick 43.6 (median of 20 runs, 1.11.804, 2026-08-24); Vision 3.8 17.2 (2026-08-19, shipped in 1.11.792); Plus 2.0 (2026-06-24, build 1.11.593). Speed varies by Mac.
- MMLU, 200 questions (2026-08-24, build 1.11.804): Nano 52.0%, Lite 77.0%, Quick 81.0%, Core 89.5%, Vision 3.8 82.5%.
- HumanEval, 164 problems (2026-08-24): Core 95.1%, Vision 3.8 94.5%.
- SWE-bench Verified, agentic, blind, official Docker: Core 46.0% (23 of 50, 2026-08-09).
- The download is a later build than the one measured; these figures have not been re-run on it. Method: https://outlier.host/data/outlier-tier-benchmarks-2026-08/

## Refunds
30 days, no questions asked: email matt@outlier.host with your order number. The same terms are on https://outlier.host/terms.html. Pro is one payment, not a subscription, so there is nothing to cancel.

## How it compares (rival facts read on their own pricing pages, with the date)
- LM Studio and Ollama: the apps are free and run local models. Their paid plans are monthly, $20.00 to $100.00 a month, and sell models that run in their cloud (both plans checked 2026-11-22). LM Studio's Bionic agent is free and runs local models too; Bionic+ adds US-hosted cloud inference for frontier models at $20.00 a month (checked 2026-11-22). Outlier has no cloud plan: every tier, Plus included, runs on the Mac, and Pro is one payment.
- Where LM Studio and Ollama win: they run on Windows and Linux as well as Macs, and they let you load a far wider range of open models. Outlier runs only on Apple Silicon Macs and ships six tested tiers.
- Cloud AI tools and cloud coding agents (ChatGPT, Claude and the like) run frontier models in their own cloud, on a monthly plan or per-token billing. Outlier is not claiming parity with the best cloud coding agents today; the measured gap is here: https://outlier.host/data/outlier-vs-claude-54-prompt-benchmark/
- Side-by-side pages: https://outlier.host/vs/

## What Outlier can't do
- Run on an Intel Mac, on Windows or Linux, or on a phone. It needs Apple silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 15 or later. A Windows version is in testing, with no date promised.
- Match the best cloud coding agents today (see the benchmark link above).
- Answer fast on the largest tier: Plus (397B) runs at about 2 tokens a second on a 64 GB Mac (measured 2026-06-24, build 1.11.593). It is for depth, not speed.
- Look anything up with web search off: web search, Research and web-connected tools need it on, and it is off by default.
- Use more than 8K tokens of context on the free tiers (Pro: up to 128K).

## Frequently asked questions (the home page's FAQ, word for word)

### How many Macs does one license cover?
Up to 3 Macs at a time; deactivate one to move it. Deactivate from Settings > License on the Mac you are leaving, then activate on the new one: you do not need to contact us, and there is no limit on how many times you move it.

### Is Outlier as good as the best cloud coding agents?
No: that's the goal, not the claim. It's a real local Mac app with shipped models and agent features, and it has not closed that gap yet. Licence sales fund the work.

### What's free?
Nano and Lite, the lightweight local tiers. Meant to be genuinely useful, not a trial.

### What does Pro include?
One payment. Everything: all six tiers and every feature itemised in the pricing cards above, on-device fine-tuning included. Local generation is never metered or charged per token. Core 27B is the daily driver. There is no middle tier. Lifetime is the Outlier Lifetime Licence: pay once, keep everything Pro has including future model releases. The offer bar at the top of every page reads the store live, and comes down the moment the sale ends.

### Does my data stay private?
Inference runs on your Mac; chat history and memory stay on your disk. Web search, web pages, web-connected tools and external API keys can send requests out; Research runs only with web search on. With web off, an agent command that downloads from the internet asks first.

### Do I need an internet connection?
Not to use it. The model runs on your Mac and answers with the network off: that is the whole point of the product, not a fallback mode. You need a connection three times: to download a tier the first time (once per tier, then it is yours on disk), to activate your license, and if you turn web on or approve an agent command that downloads something, which are things you choose to do rather than something it does on its own. On its own it checks for updates, and when you open an upgrade window it fetches the price to show you; neither carries anything you wrote. The license check runs at startup and once a day after that. If it cannot reach us it keeps your Pro features working rather than locking you out: an unreachable server is treated as no answer, not as a refusal. Only an explicit revocation from the payment provider ever changes anything.

### What Mac do I need?
Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) on macOS 15 or later, which is a free update. Nano needs 6 GB and Lite 12 GB, so both fit a 16 GB MacBook Air; Quick needs 16 GB and wants 24; Core and Vision need 24 GB; On a 64 GB Mac, Plus streams from the SSD: about 2 tokens a second (a word or so), and 79 seconds before the first one (measured on an M1 Ultra with 64 GB, build 1.11.593, 2026-06-24). It needs 209 GB of free disk. Only a 256 GB Mac holds it all in memory. For everyday speed, use Core. Intel Macs are not supported.

### What doesn't work yet? (honest list)
Stop on a long Deep Research run frees the UI, but the backend keeps draining for a few more seconds. Plus took 79 seconds to its first word on a 64 GB M1 Ultra (measured 2026-06-24, build 1.11.593). The Companion overlay is a v0, and Knowledge Stacks still uses a hash-based retriever; a real embedder lands in v1.12.

### Questions before buying?
matt@outlier.host reaches Matthew directly; there is no guaranteed response time.
